newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Tasmanian Tiger said found in Indonesia's Irian.
newsitem.headline: Tasmanian Tiger said found in Indonesia's Irian.

text.p: Villagers in Indonesia's remote and mountainous Irian Jaya province claim to have found a Tasmanian tiger living in hills around the Indonesian-Papua New Guinea border, the Antara news agency reported on Monday.

J.B. Wenas, the regent of the Jayawijaya regency, which includes the scenic Baliem Valley, told Antara that villagers and missionaries in the rugged interior of his district had reported seeing the beast attacking chickens, dogs and pigs.
"After our officials did checks in the field, it's true the animal exists, only the local people are not brave enough to capture and keep it because it is very fierce," he said.
The animal lives in caves in the Kurima sub-district around the border villages of Oksibil and Okbibab, 3,800 km (2,356 miles) east of Jakarta. It attacks domestic animals at night, he said.

The last known Tasmanian tiger, a marsupial wolf also known as the thylacine, was captured in 1933 on the Australian island state Tasmania. It died in a zoo in the state's capital Hobart in 1936. Unconfirmed sightings are often reported in Tasmania.
